AM Amin Uddin, Attorney-General with Sarwar Hossain, Deputy Attorney-General, instructed by Md Helal Amin, Advocate-on-Record—For the Petitioner. 
Md Motahar Hossain, senior Advocate, instructed by Madhumalati Chowdhury Barua, Advocate-on-Record—For the Respondents.

State -------- Petitioner
Vs.

full_judgment:
Obaidul Hassan, J: This Criminal Petition for Leave to Appeal is directed at the instance of the opposite party-petitioner against the order dated 8-8-2023 passed by the High Court Division in Criminal Miscellaneous Case No.45679 of 2023 giving direction to the accused petitioners-respondents to surrender before the Chief Metropolitan Magistrate, Dhaka within 6 (six) weeks and further directed not to arrest them by the law enforcing agency in the meantime. 

 2. The facts necessary for disposal of the Criminal Petition are that the victim's mother being the informant lodged the First Information Report (FIR) with the concerned police station on 6-8-2023 against the accused persons and the same was registered as Mohammadpur Police Station Case No.23 corresponding to GR No.1166 of 2023 under section 70 of Shishu Ain (Children Act), 2013. 

 5. Mr AM Amin Uddin, learned Attorney-General appearing for the petitioner assailing the order passed by the High Court Division contends that the impugned order is absolutely contrary to the direction given by the Appellate Division in the case of the State vs Zakaria Pintu alias Md Zakaria Pintu and others reported in 18 BLT (AD) 491. Thus, he prays for setting aside the order of the High Court Division. 

 8. It surfaces from the record that in the case in hand the respondents surrendered before the High Court Division while a direction was given to them to surrender before the learned Chief Metropolitan Magistrate, Dhaka within 6(six) weeks with a further direction to the law enforcing agency not to arrest them in the meantime. Now, the contention is that whether the High Court Division was authorized to give such direction while exercising the power of granting anticipatory bail under section 498 of the Code of Criminal Procedure, 1898. 

 9. The above crucial question was eloquently answered by this Division in the year 2010. A full-bench of six member Judges of this Division headed by the learned Chief Justice unanimously settled the said issue in the case of State vs Zakaria Pintu alias Md Zakaria Pintu and others reported in 31 BLD (AD) 20; 18 BLT (AD) 491. It is observed and held in the aforesaid case in the following manner: 

 28. Besides, the learned Judges of the High Court Division also directed the Sessions Judge, Pabna to consider the prayer of the fugitives for bail. This kind of direction is very much improper and tantamount to interfering with the discretion of the Sessions Judge, in considering the petition for bail on merit. The Sessions Judge, in considering a petition for bail is at liberty either to grant or to refuse it in his discretion, subject to merit of the case, without being influenced by an order of the High Court Division." 

 13. Pertinently, the law on grant of anticipatory bail by the High Court Division has been summed-up by this Court in the case of State vs Professor Dr. Morshed Hasan Khan and 16 others, reported in 71 DLR (AD) 364. Subsequently, referring the said decision this Division in the case of State vs Md Kabir Biswas and others in Criminal Miscellaneous Petition Nos.1432-1434 & 1441 of 2022, reported in (2022) 13 LM (AD) 13 enjoined the High Court Division and other subordinate courts to strictly follow the law and propositions propounded by this Division while dealing with anticipatory bail. 

 14. It has been observed in the case of State vs Kabir Biswas (supra) that— 

 "The impugned orders granting anticipatory bail to the respondents do not depict that while exercising the power of granting bail the High Court Division took  into consideration, inter alia, the prima facie  case placed against the accused, the gravity of the crime along with the severity of punishment prescribed for the offences  arraigned, the character, position and status of the accused with reference to the victim and  witnesses, the likelihood of the accused  fleeing from justice and repeating the offence, the possibility of his tampering with the  witnesses and obstructing the course of justice and such other grounds." 

 16. Adverting to the case in hand, the FIR discloses an allegation against the respondents of nerve-wrecking, hideous and cruel torture on the victim who is a minor girl striving to support her poverty-stricken family leaving at a remote rural area of the country working as a domestic help. The victim being a poor girl of 7 years leaving with the respondents was supposed to be in a safe shelter but to utter surprise she was being tortured mercilessly leading to the finding of a scope to flee from the custody of the accused persons. Even at one stage, the victim dared to jump from the flat situated at the 8th-storey of the building causing her severely injured. But the High court Division passed the impugned order brushing aside the prima facie allegation brought against the respondents. 

 17. The victim was working as domestic help staying at the safe shelter of the respondents. The respondent being in position to provide a safe shelter as undertaken by them cannot shred their responsibility not to happen the incident. The victim being under the shelter of the respondents the police was supposed to be in a bad need to investigate into the case unearthing the true incident through query of the respondents and other necessary means. The respondents being in a position to influence or divert fair investigation the police ought to have the opportunity to deal with the matter with full liberty. But the High Court Division without taking the nature and gravity of the arraignments into account indubitably has created clog to the investigation and also extended frustration to the victim of hideous torture. 

 22. In the premises made above, the impugned order dated 8-8-2023 passed by the High Court Division in Criminal Miscellaneous Case No.45679 of 2023 is set-aside. The order dated 21-8-2023 passed by the learned Chief Metropolitan Magistrate, Dhaka in Mohammadpur Police Station Case No.23 corresponding to GR No.1166 of 2023 under section 70 of Shishu Ain (Children Act), 2013 pursuant to the impugned order passed by the High Court Division enlarging the respondents on bail is also set-aside.
